reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports the premise that trace O/N interstitials cause phase segregation and softening in a TiVNbTa RHEA at 700°C, but it provides no evidence for the gettering mechanism, the effectiveness of Zr, or the applicability of this mechanism to a Ti-Ni-based HEA system. The hypothesis extrapolates a single observation from a chemically distinct alloy to a proposed intervention without direct support.
premises: Trace oxygen/nitrogen interstitials cause phase segregation and softening during high-temperature aging in HEAs
Depletion of strengthening interstitials from the matrix is the mechanism for softening
A getter element (Zr) can preferentially scavenge oxygen/nitrogen to form stable oxides/nitrides outside the matrix
Scavenging impurities prevents interstitial depletion and phase segregation, preserving strength
This mechanism is applicable to Ti-Ni-based HEAs based on evidence from a TiVNbTa alloy
